product_boundaries: Readiness workflow only; no compliance certification.
FDA-style sortable export language is allowed, but no FDA endorsement.
No legal advice or automated exemption determination.
Keep the product a lightweight traceability workflow layer, not ERP.

summary: GSD project initialization and Phase 1 context exist.
The CI contract gate and MockRecall contract smoke check already exist.
Batch 21 reviewed MockRecall OpenAPI examples and found no repair was needed.
Batch 22 reconciled active truth surfaces without runtime changes.
Batch 24 documented the Phase 2 MockRecall Problem Details verification scope without runtime expansion.
Phase 3 kickoff planning exists and is pending approval before implementation.
03-01A documents the provider-neutral security and persistence boundary decision without starting implementation.
Batch 27 made the MockRecall packet CSV a derived projection of the fixture record (byte-identical).
Batch 28 reshaped Problem Details into a named catalog seam with a notFound entry (byte-identical).

Batch 29 implemented the approved boundary skeleton (Variant A): the two MockRecall read routes flow through server-derived request context, deny-by-default authorization, a tenant-scoped MockRecallSource, and the Problem catalog, with idempotency/audit as uninvoked interface shapes and byte-identical runtime behavior.

Batch 34 implemented the first approved mutating write for exception-review PATCH only, using local/test fixture auth, server-derived fixture tenant identity, same-tenant reviewer RBAC, an in-memory fixture exception repository, idempotency replay/conflict handling, and append-only in-memory audit evidence.
current_state.ci_contract_gate: .github/workflows/contract-gate.yml runs npm ci, npm run api:check, npm run typecheck, npm run build, and npm run test:mock-recall:contract on push and pull request events.
current_state.mock_recall_contract_smoke: tests/mock-recall-contract-smoke.mjs verifies the current contract fixture and missing-resource Problem Details behavior against a production Next server.
current_state.mock_recall_examples_review: Batch 21 found the MockRecall detail, packet CSV, and 404 Problem Details examples aligned with runtime fixture intent; api/openapi.yaml was unchanged.
current_state.mock_recall_not_found_handlers: Runtime verified in Batch 8 and protected by the committed MockRecall contract smoke check.
current_state.mock_recall_detail_success_shape: One contract fixture exists for runtime smoke checks; no persisted or storage-backed success flow exists yet.
current_state.phase_1_goal: Maintainers can validate the API contract repeatably and rely on reviewed MockRecallDetail/packet examples before runtime expansion.
current_state.phase_2_goal: The existing not-found Problem Details behavior is protected by committed verification, with that scope documented and runtime expansion explicitly deferred.
current_state.phase_2_verification_scope: tests/mock-recall-contract-smoke.mjs protects: missing mock recall detail returns 404 application/problem+json; missing packet CSV returns 404 application/problem+json (not text/csv); the Problem Details body includes type, title, status, detail, and instance; success coverage remains the single static contract fixture only.
current_state.phase_3_goal: Establish the approved security and persistence foundation for server-derived tenant context, auth/RBAC boundaries, idempotency, persistence shape, and append-only audit evidence before production-like traceability data workflows.
current_state.phase_3_status: Boundary skeleton implemented in Batch 29 (Variant A), and the first approved mutating write is implemented in Batch 34 for PATCH /api/traceability/exceptions/{exceptionId} only. The write uses local/test fixture auth, server-derived fixture tenant identity, same-tenant reviewer RBAC, in-memory fixture repository state, idempotency replay/conflict handling, and append-only in-memory audit evidence. Phase 3 is not complete; production auth, database persistence, production RBAC, and broader workflows remain absent.
current_state.phase_3_boundary_skeleton: lib/security/request-context.ts, lib/security/authorization.ts, lib/api/mock-recall-source.ts, lib/api/route-boundary.ts, and lib/security/idempotency-audit.ts; problem.ts gained 401/403 catalog entries; both app route handlers call handleReadAction. Documented in ops/deltas/0029-boundary-skeleton.md.
current_state.phase_3_03_01a_boundary_decision: Server-derived tenant identity, request-boundary auth, deny-by-default action RBAC, tenant-scoped persistence, and paired idempotency/audit boundaries are the high-level model for future approved implementation.

remaining_absences: No production authentication provider; exception-review PATCH uses local/test fixture bearer auth only.
No persisted tenant model; tenants are server-derived fixture values only.
No production RBAC provider; exception-review PATCH enforces the same-tenant fixture reviewer role only.
No persisted audit log; exception-review PATCH appends in-memory fixture audit events only.
No persisted traceability records; exception-review PATCH mutates a deterministic in-memory fixture exception only.
No persisted or storage-backed mock-recall runtime payloads beyond the contract smoke fixture.

next_recommended_actions.action: The first approved mutating write is implemented as a fixture-only PATCH /api/traceability/exceptions/{exceptionId}. The next smallest batch should either harden focused tests/documentation around that one write or make an explicit provider-selection decision for production auth/persistence without broadening into supplier, lot/event, export, or production CSV workflows.
Do not begin auth/persistence provider selection, storage, enforcement on non-public tenants, runtime success expansion, or production CSV work until Matt approves a concrete micro-batch.

critical_do_not_expand_without_approval: Database, storage, auth, RBAC, middleware, audit log, route success behavior, generated types, package files, tests, fixtures, imports, exports, CSV generation, UI, supplier portal, OCR, ERP integration, and runtime traceability logic unless covered by the approved phase plan.
